key_insight: Omni123 unifies text-to-2D and text-to-3D generation so a single 3D-native foundation model can leverage abundant 2D image–text data to produce high-quality, geometrically consistent 3D outputs despite limited 3D training assets.
problem_solved: Addresses the scarcity of high-quality 3D data and the geometric inconsistency caused by pipelines that edit in 2D then lift to 3D, which produce under-constrained or distorted 3D results.
method: Train a unified model that supports both text→2D and text→3D generation, sharing representations so 2D supervision boosts 3D capabilities.
Combine limited 3D assets with large-scale 2D image–text pairs via cross-modal training or distillation, enforcing view and geometry consistency to regularize 3D synthesis.
Output 3D-native representations (rather than relying on post-hoc lifting of 2D edits), reducing dependence on optimization-based reconstruction and improving structural fidelity.
impact: Enables building robust text-to-3D systems without massive 3D datasets, improving geometric correctness and accelerating workflows in 3D content creation, AR/VR, simulation, and robotics.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing a single model with branching text→2D and text→3D flows and shared latent space

View-consistency diagram: multiple rendered viewpoints aligning to a coherent 3D representation
paper_title: Omni123: Exploring 3D Native Foundation Models with Limited 3D Data by Unifying Text to 2D and 3D Generation
paper_authors: Chongjie Ye, Cheng Cao, Chuanyu Pan, Yiming Hao, Yihao Zhi
